findings.reason: The protected app-local wrapper and Accepted native MyStack use the standard one-queue follow-up solution. Each push rotates exactly the older values so the queue front remains the stack top; pop, top, and empty then use only ordinary queue operations. The clear O(n)-push, O(1)-other-operation, O(n)-space implementation needs no candidate.

The former 8/64/256-value streams used 128 and 512 method calls above the source maximum of 100 and pushed values outside the legal range 1 through 9. Scaling is therefore unavailable. A verified bounded-domain certificate now proves O(n) push, O(1) pop/top/empty, O(n) storage, and O(q^2) worst aggregate work for q <= 100 calls.

The one-queue rotation invariant and per-operation complexity already match both protected forms. Alternatives and lifecycle boundaries now use explicit labels, and the Optimal summary states the exact front-preserving rotation.
